approachQuestion.prompt:
Limit Repeated Readings

An integer array readings is sorted in nondecreasing order. Modify it so its first t positions contain at most two copies of every distinct value, preserving sorted order, and return t. Keep every value that occurs once and exactly two copies of each value that occurs at least twice. Positions from t onward are ignored.

Example 1: readings=[1,1,1,2,2,3,3,3] → t=6, prefix=[1,1,2,2,3,3].
Example 2: readings=[4] → t=1, prefix=[4].
Example 3: readings=[] → t=0, prefix=[].

Constraints:
0 ≤ n=readings.length ≤ 200,000; −10^9 ≤ readings[i] ≤ 10^9.
The array can be overwritten but cannot be resized; return only the retained prefix length.
An empty array must return 0.
constraints: The array can be overwritten but cannot be resized; return only the retained prefix length.

options.text: Scan original values left to right with a write count w. Write the current value at readings[w] and increase w exactly when w<2 or the value differs from readings[w−2]. Return w.
options.feedback: Sorted order makes equal values consecutive. Two positions behind the output boundary tell whether two copies are already retained; w never exceeds the number of read values, so unread input is safe.

options.text: Copy the entire input to a helper array. Scan the copy by equal-value groups and write the first one or two values of each group into the original prefix. Return its length.
options.feedback: This returns the right prefix, including for empty input, but the full copy is unnecessary when reading and writing with a safe boundary.

options.text: Keep the current value only when the output is empty or the value differs from the immediately preceding retained value.
options.feedback: This keeps only one copy. For [5,5], both copies are required, but it returns a prefix of length 1.

options.text: Scan left to right, saving the last two ORIGINAL read values in helper variables before overwriting. Keep the first two input positions; later keep the current value only when it differs from the original value two positions earlier. Write accepted values into the prefix and return its length.
options.feedback: For sorted input, the original value at i−2 equals the current value exactly when this is at least the third occurrence in its group. Saving the last two original read values before overwriting makes this a correct fixed-state alternative; output decisions match the two-copy limit.

feedback.reason: The retained prefix, not the overwritten original prefix, records how many copies have already been accepted.
details: Read left to right. Accept the first two retained values unconditionally; later accept a value only when it differs from the retained value two positions behind the write boundary. Write accepted values into the prefix and return the boundary.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Compare Against the Retained Prefix”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the original length. Array reads/writes and comparisons cost constant time. Include the full scan; exclude the mutated input and returned length from auxiliary space, but include all helper variables and stack. No copying, recursion, hashing or resizing is used. Use a bound valid for n=0.
constraints: The array can be overwritten but cannot be resized; return only the retained prefix length.

feedback.reason: Read each original position once and retain only read/write boundaries.
details: Every original position is read once and causes at most one write. The write count never overtakes the read position. Only a read index, write count and current value are needed, including for empty input.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: A single bounded-state scan implements the quota.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: The copied-source alternative uses growing space; the fixed method does not.
The option “O((n + 1)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: No deletion shifts later values.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: The output quota can depend on values throughout the input.
